## Purpose and execution
ManimGL is a Python 3.10+ engine for programmatic mathematical animation, producing interactive previews and rendered video/image output. Its CLI loads a user scene module, selects scene classes, and executes their construction/render lifecycle. Primary entry points are `manimlib/__main__.py`, `manimlib/extract_scene.py`, and `manimlib/module_loader.py`; packaged examples live in `example_scenes.py`.

## Configuration and scene discovery
Runtime options, defaults, output locations, quality, and rendering behavior are centralized in `manimlib/config.py` and `manimlib/default_config.yml`. CLI control flows into scene extraction, which imports user Python code dynamically and identifies requested `Scene` subclasses. This is a boundary between user-authored scene modules and the engine’s internal lifecycle: `manimlib/extract_scene.py`, `manimlib/module_loader.py`, `manimlib/scene/scene.py`.

## Scene orchestration and interaction
`Scene` coordinates timeline progression: it owns mobjects, applies animations, advances frames, invokes rendering, and delegates output writing. `InteractiveScene` and embedding support a live authoring/preview workflow, while the event subsystem dispatches window input. Key paths: `manimlib/scene/scene.py`, `manimlib/scene/interactive_scene.py`, `manimlib/event_handler/event_dispatcher.py`.

## Mobject model
Mobjects are the retained scene-graph/data model: geometric primitives, text/SVG/TeX objects, images, point clouds, surfaces, coordinate systems, and mutable value-driven objects. Hierarchies and transformations originate in the base class and specialized types adapt their data for rendering. Key paths: `manimlib/mobject/mobject.py`, `manimlib/mobject/types/vectorized_mobject.py`, `manimlib/mobject/svg/tex_mobject.py`.

## Animation pipeline
Animations interpolate mobject state over scene time; composition, transformations, creation/fading, motion, and updater-based behavior provide the principal author-facing motion vocabulary. A scene schedules these objects and samples them frame by frame. Key paths: `manimlib/animation/animation.py`, `manimlib/animation/composition.py`, `manimlib/animation/transform.py`.

## GPU rendering and camera
The renderer converts mobject geometry/style data into GPU buffers, materials, pipelines, and draw calls. The camera defines frame/view/projection state; WGSL shader sources implement fills, strokes, images, surfaces, fractals, and presentation. This subsystem requires an OpenGL-capable graphics environment per project requirements. Key paths: `manimlib/renderer/renderer.py`, `manimlib/renderer/pipeline.py`, `manimlib/camera/camera.py`, `manimlib/shaders/fill.wgsl`.

## Output and external integrations
A preview window presents rendered frames, while scene file writing persists video/image output; FFmpeg is the material external dependency for video encoding. Text pipelines can invoke LaTeX (optional) and use Pango on Linux; generated assets feed back into mobject/rendering paths. Key paths: `manimlib/window.py`, `manimlib/scene/scene_file_writer.py`, `manimlib/utils/tex_file_writing.py`.

## Distribution and documentation
The project is distributed as the `manimgl` package via Python packaging metadata and has separate Sphinx documentation publishing automation. Key paths: `pyproject.toml`, `setup.py`, `.github/workflows/publish.yml`, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`.
